data.name: Abhaat
data.gender_notes: Abhaat is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: A person who radiates light and is full of brilliance and brightness. The name Abhaat carries the meaning “Glowing, Radiant” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Abhaat usually hope their child will grow to embody glowing, radiant and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A spiritual name meaning radiance and illumination, associated with the divine light of Allah.
data.etymology: Abhaat belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Glowing, Radiant.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Abhaat total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

in_arabic.name: أبهات
in_arabic.long_meaning: أبهات اسم عربي مؤنث، يُشتق من الْبَهَّة الّتي تعني الجمال والروعة والsplendor . يُستخدم هذا الاسم في الثقافة الإسلامية لتعبير عن الأنوثة و الجمال و الحُسن . لا يوجد ذِكرٌ لِاسم أبهات في القرآن الكريم. ولكنه اسم ذو معنى جميل و مُحترم في المجتمعات الإسلامية.

in_urdu.name: ابهات
in_urdu.long_meaning: ابهات ایک عربی نام ہے جو خواتین کے لیے استعمال کیا جاتا ہے۔ یہ ”بہت“ سے نکلا ہے جس کا مطلب ہے خوبصورتی، روئیت اور جلال۔ اس نام کا استعمال عربی اور فارسی کی زبانوں میں بہت عام ہے۔ یہ نام اسلامی تہذیب میں خوبصورتی، عصمت اور بلند کردار کی علامت ہے۔

in_hindi.name: अभात
in_hindi.long_meaning: अभात एक सुंदर और भारतीय समुदाय में लोकप्रिय, अरबी नाम है। यह 'बहत' से उत्पन्न हुआ है जिसका अर्थ है सुंदरता, शोभा और महिमा। इस नाम से सुंदरता, पवित्रता और उच्च आचरण की विशेषता है।

in_english.name: Abhaat
in_english.long_meaning: Abhaat is an Arabic name of feminine origin, derived from the root 'baha,' meaning beauty, splendor, and magnificence. While not explicitly mentioned in the Quran, it carries a beautiful and revered meaning within Islamic tradition. It is often associated with femininity, grace, and elegance.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Abhaat" represents a person who radiates light and is full of brilliance and brightness. In many cultures, light is often associated with knowledge, enlightenment, and wisdom. Thus, a person named Abhaat is perceived as intelligent, knowledgeable, and wise. This perception adds to their social status and respect within their community.
data.spiritual_significance: In Islamic tradition, the name "Abhaat" carries profound spiritual significance. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is reported to have said, "Allah will create a man from the dust of the earth, and that man will be called 'light' (in Arabic, 'Abnaa' Al-Nur'). He will fill the space between heaven and earth with light and guidance until the Day of Judgment." (Bukhari and Muslim). This Hadith illustrates the importance of light and guidance in Islam. Thus, the name Abhaat is a reminder of the spiritual goal of every Muslim - to seek and illuminate the path towards Allah, and to be a guiding light for others in their spiritual journeys.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Abdul-Baaqee: The servant of the Ever-Returning (to His Presence). Abhaat is a symbol of constant yearning and longing for Allah's presence, seeking His pleasure in every moment, and being eager to return to Him after each departure.

islamic_reference.note: Traditional Islamic name with deep spiritual significance in Islamic culture

historical_references.reference: Ibn Khaldun records the name Abhaat in his book 'The Muqaddimah'. He mentions that Abhaat was a Bedouin tribe living in the Hejaz region of modern-day Saudi Arabia. The tribe was known for their strong military and strategic prowess, and they played a significant role in defending the Hijaz against invasions from various other tribes and external forces, particularly the Mongols in the 13th century.

Al-Maqrizi, an Egyptian historian, also mentions the name Abhaat in his work 'The History of the Prophets and Kings'. He describes the Abhaat as a branch of the larger Azd tribe, and relates how they were one of the tribes that supported the early Islamic state during the Rashidun Caliphate in the late 7th century. They were rewarded with lands in the Hejaz region, which they governed as a semi-autonomous entity.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Abhaat' is of Islamic origin and is often used in the context of spirituality and Middle Eastern culture. In modern times, 'Abhaat' is popularly used as a hashtag on various social media platforms to represent spiritual journeys, Islamic teachings, and Middle Eastern traditions. Three popular social media platforms where 'Abhaat' is commonly used are Instagram, YouTube, and Twitter. On Instagram, 'Abhaat' is used to share visual content such as Islamic art, calligraphy, and landscapes. On YouTube, 'Abhaat' is used to search for and watch Islamic lectures, spiritual talks, and documentaries. On Twitter, 'Abhaat' is used to discuss Islamic topics, share inspirational quotes, and engage in spiritual conversations. The general trend on these platforms is to promote and share content that uplifts the spirit, deepens one's connection to their faith, and celebrates Middle Eastern culture.
